data.long_meaning: The name Ausaf is derived from the Arabic word ‘ausafa’ which means 'fortune' or 'prosperity'. This name is mentioned in the Hadith as the name of a companion of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). Ausaf represents the blessings and favors bestowed by Allah upon his believers. The name Ausaf carries the meaning “Fortune, Prosperity” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ausaf usually hope their child will grow to embody fortune, prosperity and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Khaldun's 'Muqaddimah', 14th century: In this seminal work, the historian Ibn Khaldun (1332-1406) discusses the rise and fall of Islamic dynasties and civilizations. He mentions the Banu Ausaf, a Berber dynasty in Al-Andalus (Iberian Peninsula), which ruled from the 11th to the 13th centuries. This dynasty is known for its patronage of scholarship and the arts.

Al-Maqrizi's 'Khitat', 15th century: Al-Maqrizi (1364-1442), an Egyptian historian, describes the city of Cairo under the Mamluk Sultan Qaitbey (1468-1496). He mentions a certain 'Shaykh al-Ausaf', who was a prominent Sufi scholar and teacher during that period. The name Ausaf is thus also associated with Sufi scholars in the Islamic world.
